column4: Text
Saturday. Late morning. The Hale property.
Coffee's still warm. Did you get the north fence done?
Most of it. The post by the culvert needs resetting.
The boys want to ride out to the creek after lunch. I told them to ask their father.
So they're asking me because you said yes.
I said maybe. You get to be the hero.
Dad, can I take the side-by-side to the back pasture later? I'll take these two.
Helmets. Stay off the creek bank. Back before dark.
Yes sir.
Did you know cows can walk up stairs but not down?
Let's not test that one.
I wasn't going to. Probably.
Dad, watch. Watch. It does a flip.
That's a good one, bud. Do it again.
(The long drive. Quiet out there. Quiet's good.)
(Back pasture. Cattle are bunched up by the tree line. Odd for this time of day.)
(The lake trip. Four years ago. Youngest wasn't walking yet.)
(Six months of food, rotated. She keeps the list. She's better at it than I am.)
(The county scanner. It's been silent all morning. It's never silent.)
(Cartoons. Somebody left it on again.)
(A drawing on the fridge. Five stick people and a very large dog. We don't have a dog.)
(The tractor hydraulics are still in pieces. Next weekend.)
(Gate, drive, barn, east field. Nothing but cattle.)
That's every channel.
Phones too.
Is this it?
Doesn't matter what it is. We do it the way we practiced.
Hey. Look at me. You've got your brothers. Hallway, away from the windows.
Dad, what's happening?
I don't know yet. That's why we're careful.
Shop. Now.
Your code or mine?
Mine.
Zero six one four. In case you've gotten old.
Zero. Six. One. Four.
Lights are coming up. Everything's where we left it.
Plates are on the left rack. Check your mag before you seat it.
Optic's still zeroed. Radios are on channel four.
(Rifle. Function check. Good.)
(Sidearm.)
Here. Arms up.
(Six mags. Same as always.)
Radio check.
Loud and clear.
Take the big kit. I've got the other one.
(Go bags. Three days each.)
(Water, filters, batteries. Hope we don't need them.)
I'm up. You?
Up.
Vehicle! Coming up the drive, coming in hot!
Hale! Hale, don't shoot. It's Mercer!
Hands where I can see them. All of you.
It's us. It's just us.
Whose blood is that?
Not ours. Not all of it.
Inside. Keep your hands out of your pockets.
There are armed teams moving through the county. No markings. They hit the substation on Route 9 and the checkpoint at the county line.
I lost two deputies. I don't even know who they were shooting at.
I got three orders in an hour. Evacuate. Shelter in place. Then a federal liaison telling me to report to the courthouse with every department head.
Nobody who called me would give a name.
Don't go to the courthouse.
You keep saying that like you know something.
I know enough to come here.
How long have you known something was coming?
Not long enough to call you. I'm sorry.
Ask me later. When there's a later.
(Approach road: SAFE. Shop bay: SAFE.)
Are those explosives?
They're a deterrent.
That's not an answer.
It's the one I've got.
I'll get the boys. Close the gate.
Why are we in here?
Because it's the safest room we have. Listen to your dad.
Take this. Channel four. You keep your brothers calm.
Do not open this door. Not for anybody. You only answer to Mom or me.
What if somebody says...
Mom. Or me.
Mom or Dad. Okay.
Dad?
I know, bud. Stay with your brother.
Sealed.
They'll be okay.
I know. Say it anyway.
Hale. Engines. A lot of them.
Gate camera.
Black SUVs. No plates. No markings.
They're not in a hurry.
They don't need to be.
Attention, Hale residence. This is the National Continuity Directorate.
We are here for Sheriff Mercer, Mayor Vale, and Nathan Cole.
Residents of this property are not currently the target of federal action.
Disable your property defenses. Open the gate. Send the three men to the road.
Mr. Hale. We are aware of the countermeasures on your approach road. Place them in a safe state.
How do they know your name? How do they know about...
Who the hell are these people?
National Continuity Directorate. It's supposed to be part of continuity-of-government planning. Classified.
It operates when the normal structure is considered compromised. Or irrelevant.
Who runs it?
Nobody can tell you. No public presence. No oversight anyone can point to. No chain of command on paper.
They're what shows up when the agencies stop mattering.
Then we go out. If it's us they want...
You walk out that gate, you don't come back. You know that.
Nobody's coming out.
Understood.
Gate's down. They're coming up the drive!
Hale. The panel.
(Approach road: ARMED.)
Not yet. Let them bunch up at the culvert.
They're stopping. They're dismounting. Now.
My God.
That won't stop them. They'll regroup.
Movement at the wrecks. Hale, drop the wall!
Stay low between shots. The plate is your friend.
I've got the left side of the drive.
More vehicles on the drive!
Tree line, west side! They're moving in the trees!
They're moving down the east side of the shop!
East window! Hale, swing right, I've got the port!
More of them. There's more of them.
We can't hold this. Hale, we can't hold this!
Armored. Two of them.
Dad? It's really loud. Are you okay?
Stay put, buddy. Mom or me.
Grenade! Move!
That wasn't us.
Who the hell was that?
Vehicles in the west field. East field too.
More of them?
No. Look who they're shooting at.
Residence secure.
Commander.
Commander?
Hale. Who are these people?
We're here to recover anyone at the residence not declared hostile.
Your family?
Vault. Three boys.
And these three?
They're with us.
Then they're non-hostile. Confirmed.
Directorate will have a second element inbound. We're not here when it arrives.
Mom!
Hey, hey. We're okay. We're okay.
Dad. Why did they call you Commander?
Later.
Dad...
Later. I promise.
Mount up. We move now.
Family in the lead vehicle. Civilians in the second.
Everything?
Everything.
Then do it.
